decisions.reason: A reference electrometer sits at the core of the firm's decades of dosimetry and calibration knowledge, and it is featured on the home page, so the firm can fully absorb and refine it.
Oncology risk management software builds on the firm's software integration skills and its move toward combining machine and patient QA, and its own page for two years points to continued commitment.
A CT image quality phantom draws on the firm's existing imaging QA and measurement expertise, so early results are easy to interpret and improve.

Mammography is further from the firm's radiotherapy dosimetry core, but its physicists and imaging QA know-how give it enough related knowledge to learn from early results, so it is kept for now despite higher risk.
This second distant mammography phantom overlaps with Product D, which slightly raises the chance of consolidation, yet it is too early to judge and it fits the firm's expanding imaging QA portfolio.
Imaging QA instruments build on the firm's measurement and calibration capabilities and support its broad offering, so the firm can readily assimilate feedback on them.
